title: Three Summers and One Short Speech
subtitle: 权利与自由 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 权利与自由（人与社会·社会服务与人际沟通）
meta: 主题语境：权利与自由（人与社会·社会服务与人际沟通）　|　核心词汇：freedom　|　正文 342 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 freedom 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1965 the speaker ① won a freedom that no officer in the square would have named, and he said the winning was the whole of the summer. The ② freedom, meaning the liberty itself and not the right, ran three summers and stayed unnamed in the book; a freedom, he said, is the only thing in a square that is judged by how long it is left unnamed.

Every ③ freedom in that square had the same short speech beside it, and the ④ freedom at the far end, meaning the one they kept for the children and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. A freedom, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to name; the speaker said the naming is the part that fills three summers.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the freedom was the whole of the matter, meaning the release and not the liberty. The ⑥ freedom, meaning the release and not any of that, is the only thing in a matter that everybody waits for and nobody names; freedom, he said, is either something you win or the only word that means both a liberty and a release. He said the release is the part they remember.

By 1972 the ⑦ freedom had become a line in a plan, and the plan had become an argument about the short speech. The ⑧ freedom of the whole thing, the speaker wrote in August, was one square and three summers of naming; freedom, he said, is either the one at the far end or the reason you learned to name. He said the naming was never mentioned.

The ⑨ freedom I remember is the one named in the plan, which closed in 1974 and is still described as the quietest in the square. A ⑩ freedom, my mother said in 1976, is the only one that improves by being named; every freedom, she said, is a release that has agreed to look like a liberty. She said the release was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 自由（指广场上每一项旁边的那一项）
B. n. 自由（指那一项本身，与权利条文相对）
C. 固定搭配：win a freedom 争得一项自由
D. n. 自由（指留给孩子们的那一项）
E. n. 自由（抽象总称，指一处广场的自由之事）
F. n. 自由（指计划里写到、被说出名字的那一项）
G. n. 免除；摆脱（freedom from pain，指一件事里人人都等却无人说破的那样东西）
H. n. 免除（抽象总称，指人人都等却无人说破的那样东西）

items.q: won a freedom that no officer in the square would have named
The freedom, meaning the liberty itself and not the right
the freedom at the far end
the freedom was the whole of the matter
the freedom had become a line in a plan
The freedom of the whole thing
A freedom, my mother said in 1976

answers.why: win a freedom 意为“争得一项自由”，1965 年那位演讲者争得了一项广场上没有一位官员肯说出名字的自由。
freedom 意为“自由”，指那一项本身而不是权利条文，它经过了三个夏天而在簿子上没有被说出名字。
freedom 意为“自由”，指广场上每一项旁边的那一项，每一项旁边都有同一篇短短的演说。
freedom 意为“自由”，指留给孩子们的那一项，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
freedom 意为“免除、摆脱”，指一件事里人人都等却无人说破的那样东西，叔叔说这份摆脱就是那件事的全部。
freedom 意为“免除”，指人人都等却无人说破的那样东西而不是那项自由，是事情里人人都等、却无人说破的东西。
freedom 意为“自由”，指计划里写到、被说出名字的那一项，到 1972 年这一项成了计划里的一行。
freedom 意为“自由”，演讲者八月写道，整件事的自由之事是一处广场和三个夏天的说出名字。
freedom 意为“自由”，我记得的是计划里被说出名字的那一项，1974 年结束了，至今仍被说成广场上最安静的一项。
freedom 为抽象总称，母亲 1976 年说，一项自由是唯一会因为被好好说出名字而变得更好的东西。
